notes: New Zealand + Thailand routes reverified against current first-party sources. Skinny now uses Skinny direct terms rather than Spark proxy; 2degrees current 365-day rule is resolved; AIS SIM2Fly keeps identity-registration and continuous-roaming limits explicit.

routes.acquisitionSummary: Skinny Prepaid offers a $0 eSIM and a $2 physical Trio SIM. Current Skinny terms require adding credit at least once every 12 months; current top-up amounts start at NZ$5. New SIMs must be activated on a New Zealand network before roaming, so this is not a direct overseas-first acquisition route.

keep.action: Add credit at least once every 12 months. Current Skinny top-up amounts start at NZ$5, so NZ$5/year is the current minimum direct top-up model; recheck before each renewal because prices can change.

routes.chinaActivation: BLOCKER for overseas-first acquisition: Skinny states new SIMs must be activated on New Zealand networks before a roaming pack can be used. Physical SIM and eSIM are both available, but first activation should not be assumed to work from China or another overseas location.
routes.kyc: The reviewed ordinary Skinny prepaid activation flow does not state an identity-document verification step. Do not generalize this into a jurisdiction-wide no-ID claim; the hard current constraint is first activation on a New Zealand network.
routes.payment: Skinny terms support top-up by Visa/Mastercard credit or debit card, voucher and other accepted methods; issuer/country acceptance should be checked at payment time.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: Skinny Global Roaming supports sending and receiving text messages where the overseas network supports the service. New SIMs must first be activated on New Zealand networks.
routes.holdReason: HOLD for typical overseas-only users because a new Skinny SIM/eSIM must first be activated on a New Zealand network before roaming; the retention rule itself is now directly verified.
routes.tariffSummary: $0 eSIM / $2 physical SIM; current top-ups start at NZ$5 and at least one credit addition is required each 12 months. First activation must occur on a New Zealand network.
guideSteps: Acquire a Skinny eSIM or physical SIM.
Activate the new SIM on a New Zealand network before relying on roaming.
Add at least NZ$5 credit before each 12-month no-top-up window expires; recheck the current minimum before renewal.

routes.acquisitionSummary: 2degrees currently offers new Prepay customers a physical SIM or eSIM with free delivery and adds the NZ$8 Monthly Plan to the new SIM. Current official Prepay guidance requires a minimum NZ$10 top-up every 365 days to keep the account active.

keep.action: Top up at least NZ$10 every 365 days to keep the Prepay account active. Current official guidance says unused balance is forfeited and the SIM expires if this is not done.

routes.chinaActivation: Current official material supports online eSIM/SIM ordering and eSIM QR installation, but the reviewed sources do not establish that a brand-new Prepay line can complete first activation from overseas. Roaming requires an active Prepay plan, so do not rely on overseas-first activation without a fresh explicit provider statement.
routes.kyc: The reviewed ordinary 2degrees Prepay activation/help flow does not state an identity-document verification step. This is provider-flow evidence only, not a blanket legal claim about New Zealand prepaid registration.
routes.payment: Prepay top-up is supported in the 2degrees app and online; current minimum top-up is NZ$10. Card/Online EFTPOS/voucher methods are documented, with issuer/country acceptance to be checked at payment time.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: 2degrees documents Prepay roaming and text use abroad. Its current Daily Roaming trigger list names sending a text but does not name receiving a text as a trigger; exact inbound-SMS charging and service-specific OTP reliability should not be overstated.
routes.holdReason: The stale retention-terms blocker is resolved, but overseas-first activation of a brand-new Prepay line is not established by the reviewed current official material. Keep as HOLD for the typical overseas-only acquisition use case.
routes.tariffSummary: New SIM/eSIM currently starts with the NZ$8 Monthly Plan; minimum NZ$10 top-up every 365 days keeps Prepay active. Overseas-first activation remains unverified.
guideSteps: Order a new physical SIM or eSIM with the current Prepay entry plan.
Do not assume a brand-new line can first-activate abroad; establish activation before relying on roaming.
Top up at least NZ$10 every 365 days to prevent account/SIM expiry.

routes.acquisitionSummary: AIS currently advertises the SIM2Fly 1-Year Global roaming SIM at 2,699 baht promotional price (regular/terms price 2,799) for 15GB over 365 days. SIM2Fly can first-activate in Thailand or a supported destination including China, but SIM registration/identity verification is required and long-term continuous roaming has explicit limitations.

keep.action: AIS says topping up can add SIM validity and On-Top packages can add validity days, but the reviewed current sources do not establish the cheapest durable number-retention top-up ladder beyond the packaged validity. Do not treat the 365-day data-package price as the minimum annual keep-alive cost.

routes.chinaActivation: First activation is allowed in Thailand or any supported SIM2Fly country; China (including Tibet) is listed for the Global package. The activated SIM must be used in a designated country within 60 days or the roaming package can be voided. Identity registration still applies.
routes.kyc: SIM registration is required. AIS states all mobile numbers must be registered; foreign nationals can use passport information for registration/verification. The prior passport-free wording is removed.
routes.payment: SIM2Fly is sold through AIS online and retail channels; exact foreign-card acceptance for the selected purchase channel should be verified at checkout.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: AIS SIM2Fly documentation says calls and SMS can be received normally while abroad, and China is a supported destination. However, AIS reserves the right to suspend roaming after more than 60 days of continuous roaming, so long-term inbound SMS/OTP continuity must not be assumed.
routes.holdReason: HOLD for long-term overseas number-retention/OTP use: exact minimum post-package number-retention economics are unresolved and AIS reserves the right to suspend roaming after more than 60 days of continuous roaming. Identity registration is also required.
routes.tariffSummary: Current 1-Year Global card shows 2,699 THB promo versus 2,799 THB terms price for 15GB/365d. This is a roaming-data product price, not a proven minimum annual number-retention cost.
guideSteps: Complete AIS SIM registration/identity verification; foreign nationals should expect passport-based verification.
First-activate in Thailand or a supported SIM2Fly destination such as China and use it in a designated country within 60 days.
Do not rely on continuous roaming beyond 60 days or on a fixed post-year keep-alive cost until AIS publishes/validates the relevant retention mechanics.
